headline: Your The Modern Data Company waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing warehouse-backed enterprises into the right DataOS offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Darpan Shah.
productSummary: DataOS is The Modern Data Company's data operating system: a data activation layer that sits on Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, lakes, and catalogs the enterprise already runs. It turns that stack into governed, reusable, AI-ready data products. No migration. No rip-and-replace. Pay as you go, or enterprise yearly. Headquartered in Palo Alto, with offices in San Jose, Indore, Hyderabad, and Bangalore.
coreInsight: Darpan already sells the missing activation layer on top of the warehouse the buyer paid for. That is still the live product at themoderndatacompany.com and tmdc.io. The one TAM is enterprises on Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery. The one routing signal is the public overlay stack BuiltWith returns with that warehouse, because it is observable without a second enrichment hop and it tells you whether they already bought a catalog, parked metrics in a BI tool, are still running pipeline-per-use-case, or have storage and no OS.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is the overlay on the warehouse
sections.takeaway: A company's BuiltWith stack already names Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery, plus the catalog, semantic layer, or pipeline tools sitting on top. That overlay is stronger than a headcount guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every warehouse account
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Catalog and governance point solutions go first, then semantic/metrics layers, then pipeline-per-use-case tooling, then every remaining warehouse.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each overlay gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Catalog buyers get a teardown of point-solution spend. Semantic stacks get a company-brain brief. Pipeline shops get a 4-to-6-week product map. The rest get the AI-Readiness Scorecard.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Save money, save time, activate AI, on the same routes
sections.takeaway: The list is always warehouse-backed enterprises, aimed at CDO / CIO / CTO / Head of Data. Industry is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the tool they already run
sections.takeaway: Notice the catalog, Looker model, or dbt project, poke the queue that stack creates, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the catalog overlay first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already paid for governance and still wait on tickets. Prove reply density, then roll semantic, pipeline, and the scorecard catch-all.

signalReasons: BuiltWith directories for Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery are the TAM DataOS names on its own FAQ, in one pull.
The same pull returns Collibra, Alation, Atlan, Looker, Cube, dbt, Airflow, and Fivetran, which is enough to route without a second enrichment hop.
The ladder maps to live DataOS copy: replace fragmented point solutions, put semantics inside the data product, compress 30-32 weeks to 4-6, and add the activation layer the warehouse is missing.
Industry pages (manufacturing, retail and CPG, financial services, public sector, distribution) are a scrape filter. They are not a second waterfall.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Catalog overlay
tiers.trigger: BuiltWith or Wappalyzer shows Collibra, Alation, Atlan, Informatica, Immuta, Privacera, Purview, OvalEdge, or data.world on Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery
tiers.pain: They already bought a catalog or governance tool, so the gap is budgeted. The catalog still sits around the data. Access takes tickets, and point solutions pile up next to the warehouse they already paid for.
tiers.valueProp: DataOS can replace fragmented catalog and governance point solutions, or layer over them. Governance, lineage, and policies live inside the data product. A leading UK bank on Modern's financial-services page cut metadata cataloging 160x and PII tagging 700x.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. They already pay for the gap a catalog did not close.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Semantic / metrics layer
tiers.trigger: Looker, Cube, AtScale, or dbt Semantic Layer / MetricFlow detected, and no catalog overlay
tiers.pain: Metrics live in a BI or metrics tool. The same KPI shows up differently in the next dashboard, and an AI agent cannot inherit that LookML. Definitions never made it into the data.
tiers.valueProp: DataOS puts a unified semantic layer inside every data product. Set once, used by analysts, apps, and AI agents. MCP-native. No extra pipeline so people and models share one definition.
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. They already tried to standardize metrics. The definition still sits in a tool.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Pipeline-per-use-case
tiers.trigger: dbt Cloud, Airflow, Fivetran, Airbyte, Prefect, or Dagster detected, and no catalog or semantic overlay already routed
tiers.pain: Transform and orchestration are live, so each new request is still its own pipeline. The data team is a queue. A use case still takes a quarter.
tiers.valueProp: Modern's homepage puts the typical path at 30-32 weeks and DataOS at 4-6 (8x). Data products, built once, reused. Lenovo: 80% faster development cycles, 9x faster time to implementation, no platform replacement. Up to 50% lower data costs.
tiers.replyDensity: Good. The stack proves they are still in the long path DataOS exists to shorten.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Missing activation layer
tiers.trigger: Every remaining Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery account in the TAM
tiers.pain: The warehouse is live and the operating system is not. AI and the business wait on the same engineering queue. The gap is activation, not storage.
tiers.valueProp: DataOS is that layer. No rip-and-replace. Pay as you go with no upfront fees, or enterprise if volume is high. First data products in weeks. Homepage: 90% faster data activation, 10x faster decisions.
tiers.dataSource: Warehouse TAM after higher tiers route out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM.

campaigns.strategy: Name the metrics tool and the conflicting-KPI problem, then offer a data-product semantic layer

campaigns.name: Agents cannot inherit LookML

campaigns.name: Pipeline-to-Product Map
campaigns.filter: dbt Cloud, Airflow, Fivetran, Airbyte, Prefect, or Dagster, no higher overlay
campaigns.strategy: Name the transform tool and the 30-32 week path, then offer reusable data products in 4-6 weeks

campaigns.name: Maintenance budget variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep the pipeline tool in the first line. Lead with 70-80% of engineering budget on maintenance and 50% lower data costs.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the product map. Same exclusive route, cost language.

campaigns.name: AI-Readiness Scorecard
campaigns.strategy: Notice the warehouse, name the missing activation layer, offer the scorecard Modern already publishes
campaigns.overview: Catch-all coverage so every scraped warehouse still gets one route. Scorecard is the tiny yes.

campaigns.name: No-rip-and-replace starter
campaigns.strategy: Lead with no upfront fees and keep-the-warehouse. Do not change routing.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the scorecard. Still exclusive catch-all, still one TAM.

launchPlan: Pull BuiltWith Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery directories with overlay fields in the same export. Suppress already_on_dataos when visible.
Resolve CDO / CIO / CTO / Head of Data titles only after the domain is routed. Apollo last.
Launch Tier 1 Catalog Overlay first. Smallest list, sharpest spend signal. Save-money copy as the control, save-time as the A/B on the same list.
Add Tier 2 Semantic / Company-Brain once Looker, Cube, and dbt-semantic merge tags are clean. Then Tier 3 Pipeline-to-Product.

Turn on the AI-Readiness Scorecard catch-all last so every remaining warehouse account still has a route. Keep industry as a merge tag, not a campaign split, until one overlay tier is clearly working.
